Subject: ACME compliance: certification gateways & audit plan sync

Hi Mina & Marissa —

ACME's security team looped me this morning to request a consolidated view of what we can deliver for their procurement and pre-assessment: SIG/CAIQ export, SOC 2 artifacts they can consume, and a short FedRAMP readiness statement. They want to know:

- What evidence we can provide this week vs. what requires sampling (e.g., controls that need logs or retained traces).
- Expected turnaround time for a CAIQ/SIG full response vs. a high-level summary.
- Any blockers for FedRAMP pre-assessment (network isolation, audit logging retention, personnel access lists).

Do we have a recommended owner list for ACME (who pulls which evidence) and a minimal handoff package we can share with procurement by EOD Friday? I attached the ACME SIG they sent earlier — can you confirm what we can fill in from existing artifacts.

If useful, can we set a 20-minute sticky call today to triage? I can host.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME compliance: certification gateways & audit plan sync

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads up. Quick summary below and I attached an evidence matrix that maps our artifacts to SIG/CAIQ/FedRAMP items. High level:

- Immediate deliverables (available this week):
  - Control narratives for access control, change management, encryption-at-rest (doc templates)
  - SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) + SOC 2 bridge letter (if requested)
  - System architecture diagram and network zone descriptions

- Sampling / 2-4 week items:
  - Retained audit log samples and log retention policy enforcement records (needs engineering pull)
  - 90-day evidence for incident response runbook execution (we can provide summaries, but raw artifacts require katana-access)

- FedRAMP blockers to call out now:
  - We do not currently publish a formal FedRAMP scoping statement; for pre-assessment we can provide a readiness checklist but full FedRAMP will require additional documentation on IL2/IL4 boundary controls and a third-party assessment.
  - Network isolation for some dedicated deployments is achievable but must be validated per-customer (VPC peering configs).

Owner recommendations:
  - Mina: SOC 2 artifacts + control narratives + evidence matrix (attached: evidence_matrix_ACME.csv)
  - Marissa: ISO mapping and architecture diagrams
  - Engineering (cc Vivek): log samples & retention enforcement (request to devops team)

If you can get Procurement/ACME to accept a "pre-assessment handoff" package (SOC 2 redacted + SIG draft + architecture + evidence matrix), we can ship that by EOD Friday. Otherwise we should be explicit about the 2-4 week cadence for sampled items.

I can join a 20-minute call at 11:30 PST.

— Mina
Mina Haddad | Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: evidence_matrix_ACME.csv (CSV)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Jordan / Mina —

Adding a couple ISO/architecture notes:

- ISO 27001 mapping: we have control mappings in our internal Confluence space. I can export the control-to-evidence sheet today (will attach the PDF). That will cover policy-level artifacts requested in CAIQ/SIG.
- Architecture: updated sequence diagram for private deployment + dedicated pools is current as of Aug 2026; I will attach the diagram (redacted hostnames).
- For FedRAMP readiness statement: recommend a short paragraph that we can include in the handoff package clarifying that Redwood is in early readiness (no JAB/P-ATO) and that customer-specific boundary scoping will be required. I can draft that paragraph.

One ask for Procurement: if they need continuous logging proof, ask them whether aggregated log samples (redacted timestamps) are sufficient or if they require raw event dumps — we should avoid handing over raw logs unless a DPA/contract clause is signed.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachment: architecture_private_pool_aug2026.pdf (PDF); attachment to follow via Drive link

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick reply and the proposed deliverables. A couple clarifying items from our side before you compile the package:

1) For SOC 2 redacted reports, can you also provide the control matrix mapping that ties SOC 2 controls to SIG/CAIQ items? That will accelerate procurement review.
2) For log samples: aggregated/redacted samples are acceptable for now; procurement will escalate if they need raw feeds (we will coordinate a formal NDA/DPA).
3) Timeline: procurement needs the pre-assessment handoff by next Tuesday (2026-09-08) to keep our internal sourcing window. If Redwood cannot deliver by then, please flag which items will fall into the two-week sampling window.

If helpful, we can take the SOC 2 redacted + evidence matrix as first pass and move forward with contract terms in parallel.

Regards,
ACME Security Team
